summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Teleport to a far-away structure such as a woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Observe if the chunks near you are loading in.
3. If the chunks are not loading in, reload chunks using F3 + A and observe again.
4. If chunks still do not load after reloading, teleport closer to the structure containing naturally generated allays and repeat step 3.
5. If chunks continue to fail to load even when close to the structure with naturally generated allays, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
6. Observe that the F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and no further chunk loading occurs.
7. Attempt to save your world; note that saving will not be possible if chunks are not loading in, leading to a forced crash of the game (no data will be saved).
8. Document the observation by taking a screenshot or noting down the coordinates for reference.
Observed Behavior:
When loading chunks containing structures with naturally generated allays, the server hangs and the game stops responding. Teleporting a few thousand blocks away causes all chunk loading to cease, while the F3 menu still functions but is stuck showing an internal server tick at 18ms, preventing further chunk loading. Commands and UI elements like the gamemode switcher become non-functional. Occasionally, 2-8 chunks may load if you are not inside a structure with naturally generated allays. Attempting to save the world while this issue occurs will fail, forcing a game crash without saving any data. Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this problem, nor does visiting a woodland mansion that lacks naturally generated allays. Only structures with naturally generated allays trigger this bug.

To reproduce the issue:
1) Teleport to a distant structure such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost.
2) Observe if nearby chunks are loading.
3a) If chunks aren't loading, attempt to reload them using F3+A; check if they load now.
3b) If reloading doesn’t work, ensure you have teleported close enough to the structure containing allays and try again.
4a) If chunks still do not load after these steps, this bug has been successfully reproduced.
4b) If chunks load correctly, it's possible that your Minecraft version is incorrect; ensure you are using version 22w13a as later snapshots may have patched the issue.

To exit when this happens:
- DO NOT USE F3+C or ALT+F4.
- On Windows: Use Task Manager to end the "OpenJDK Platform binary" task.
- On Linux: Open a terminal and use `kill` followed by the process ID, or use `killall`, `xkill`, or System Monitor.
- On MacOS: Press and hold Command+Option+Shift, then press Esc to force quit the application.

These steps are specific to certain conditions; if new conditions arise, additional instructions should be provided.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting near structures containing naturally generated allays, chunks should load normally without causing the server to hang or game to stop responding. The F3 menu and UI elements should function as expected, allowing for chunk reloading and other interactions. Commands should work, and saving the world should be possible without force-crashing the game.
